analysis:
The only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is one added bullet at head line 1274, in the `darkbloom status` output list. It says App Attest serving authorization can stay visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice requires a matching fresh coordinator decision. It also says the same distinction applies to both doctor summaries and links to the provider-authorization reference. This is documentation only: no code, permission, key handling, wire protocol or deployment setting changes.

I checked it against the App Attest threat entries in the supplied index (A-015, A-016, TB-011, T-053, T-057) and found no control weakened. The statement is consistent with the stated principle that a cached verdict or an unexpired lease is not independent proof, and that MDM-removal guidance requires current evidence. It makes no claim of eligibility, revocation or secrecy that would overclaim trust. This is the safer direction, since it discourages premature MDM removal (T-057).

Limits: TB-011 and T-053 were oversized or not shown in full, and the linked ../reference/provider-authorization.md is not in the batch. I could not confirm the bullet matches the platform-owned EvaluateAuthorization behavior, or that the referenced doctor code implements the stated distinction. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. The rest of the supplied base text (sandbox setup, addon hold, prefix cache, models) is unchanged context. I did not re-evaluate pre-existing items such as the T-061 installer trust or the T-041 cache posture.
